This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.

Due to the said impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries, thereafter immediately shifted to Government Hospital,
Dibbur, wherein he took treatment as inpatient, for which he has spent a sum of Rs.4,00,000/-
towards medical and nourishment expenses.

3. At the time of the accident he was aged about 24 years, hale and healthy, he was studying 2nd year LLB, due to the said accident, he is not able to lead a normal life and he has suffered loss of academic year.
Out of this SCCH-5 accident crime No.169/2021 is registered against the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-EC-2682 before the Chikkaballapur Rural Police.
Respondent No.1 is the insurer, respondent No.2 is owner of the said motor cycle, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
4.
On service of notice, R1/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and denied the averments of the petition.

Further submitted that, rider of the vehicle has no driving license at the time of accident,hence police have filed charge sheet against the rider for the offences punishable under Sec.3, 181 of M.V.Act.
He seeks protection under Sec.149(2) of M.V.Act.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.

Claim SCCH-5 made by the petitioner is higher,
hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5. Respondent No.2/owner has appeared and filed written statement denying averments of the petition, further claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.

Further stated that he is registered owner of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 40-EC-2682 and the said vehicle was insured with respondent No.1 with policy No.P0021000100/4102/756947 which is valid since 19.03.2021 to 18.03.2022.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

sentences.text:
On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
SCCH-5 1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 28.09.2021 at abut 10.45 a.m. when petitioner was travelling as pillion rider on motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-EC-2682 near Golluchinnapanahalli Village, Chikkaballapura Taluk, Bengaluru at that time, one motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-43-S-3523 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?

2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

7. In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW-1, examined Dr.Shailesh A.V.Rao, Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon at Padmashree Diagnostics as PW-2 and marked 17 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.17 and closed his evidence.
On the other SCCH-5 hand, Assistant Legal Manager of respondent No.1 company is examined as RW-1 and exhibited Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2 and closed his evidence.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1:- In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as SCCH-5 Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of vehicle seizure mahazar is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.6 and copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.6.

sentences.text: Further to substantiate the petitioner case, he examined one Doctor as PW-2.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 and records those have marked i.e., as FIR, complaint, sketch, spot mahazar, vehicle seizure mahazar, IMV Report and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 28.09.2021 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
11.

Per contra, the Assistant Legal Manager in respondent No.1 company is examined as RW-1 and he has exhibited authorization letter marked as Ex.R.1 and SCCH-5 copy of policy marked as Ex.R.2 and respondent No.1 has not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 28.09.2021 at about 10.45 a.m. while he was proceeding as a pillion rider on motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-EC-2682 ridden by its rider on Golluchinnappanahalli Village, Chikkaballapura Taluk, Bengaluru.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
12. On the other hand, the police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-EC-2682.
SCCH-5

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:-
As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained right sided acute subdural hemotoma, multiple brain contusions and severe brain edema with affected basal cisterns.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.8, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.9 issued by Apuva Mother and Child Hospital, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient since 28.09.2021 to 13.10.2021, once again he was admitted as inpatient from 09.02.2022 to 15.02.2022, totally for 21 days.
SCCH-5 14.
Ofcourse, PW-2 Dr.Shailesh A.V.Rao, Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon at Padmashree Diagnostis, Vijayanagar, Bengaluru is examined as PW-2.

To substantiate his evidence, he has exhibited OPD records marked as Ex.P.14, neuro psychological assessment report marked as Ex.P.15, mini mental state examination report marked as Ex.P.16 and skull X-ray report marked as Ex.P.17 and he has assesssed whole body disability at the rate of 20% which is permanent.

In cross- examination he has categorically admitted that, he has not treated the petitioner and he has not consulted treated Doctor and also he has assessed disability with reference to 2018 guidelines.

Under such circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also by relying on citation reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajay Kumar,
SCCH-5 the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 20% for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

The said whole body disability is taken into consideration, as Pavan Kumar vs Magma Hdi Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32624895/
4 the petitioner has caused injury to his head and facing neurological problems.
15.

Under such circumstances,
considering the educational qualification of the petitioner and possibilities of earning his livelihood in future and with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.14,250/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

once again he was admitted as inpatient from 09.02.2022 to 15.02.2022, totally for 21 days.

For the said period he is entitled for the loss of income as per the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner should be taken into consideration i.e., Rs.14,250/- p.m.

sentences.text: Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the income of said quantum for the period he was admitted as inpatient in SCCH-5 the hospital.

So petitioner is entitled for Rs.9975/- towards loss on income during laid up period.
18.
Further admittedly petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.12 medical bills for Rs.5,79,049/-.
On perusal of the said bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for this treatment is considered.
Further on perusal of Ex.P.8 in which Doctor who have treated i.e., Dr.Krishnaprasad has categorically stated that, petitioner has sustained grievous injury out of the accident caused on 28.09.2021.
So as per Ex.P.8 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained right FTP acute SDH with diffuse brain injury, which is grievous in nature.

Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Chandrashekar C.L. for the offences punishable under Sec.181 of M.V.Act,
Sec.279, 338 of IPC and Sec.8 of M.V.Act.
So the said charge sheet materials and SCCH-5 evidence of PW-1 and PW-2
clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Accordingly petitioner Pavan Kumar vs Magma Hdi Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32624895/
5 is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.5,79,049/-.

sentences.text: Per contra, except denial in the written statement and oral evidence of RW-1, respondents have not taken any endeavors to step into witness box nor to prove the allegations as alleged in the written statement.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, merely respondents have filed written statement and they have denied entire case of the petitioner are all not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case, because it is bounden duty of him to prove the defence as taken in the written statement.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for medical bills and other compensation as stated below.
SCCH-5 20.

Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-
Sl.No.
Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of Future Income 6,15,600-00 2.
Pain and sufferings 15,000-00 3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,000-00 attendant charges 4.
Medical Expenses 5,79,049-00 5. Loss of amenities in life 15,000-00 6. Loss of income during laid up 9,975-00 period Total 12,49,624-00 21.
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.12,49,624/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

22. In the case on hand, respondent No.1 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.P0021000100/4102/756947 which is valid for the SCCH-5 period from 19.03.2021 to 18.03.2022, the alleged accident was occurred on 28.09.2021 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Further rider of the motor cycle by name Chandrashekar C.L. did not possess valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident, accordingly charge sheet is filed against him for the offences punishable under Sec.181, 3 of M.V.Act.

Under such circumstances, naturally respondent No.2/owner is liable to pay the compensation in favour of petitioners, but as per the observations made and findings given by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s. Swarna Singh and other reported in AIR 2004 SC 1531 and in case of Pappu and another V/s. Vinod Kumar Lamba and another reported in AIR 2018 SC 592, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, it is just and SCCH-5 necessary to issue directions against respondent No.1/Insurance Company to satisfy the petitioner by way of depositing the award amount within 60 days from the date of this order with interest at the rate of Pavan Kumar vs Magma Hdi Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32624895/
6 6% p.a. and recover from the respondent No.2/owner through process of law, because this accident was occurred on 28.09.2021 i.e., prior to the amendment to M.V.Act i.e., 01.04.2022

Accordingly, I have answered above Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:
For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

:: 
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.12,49,624/- (Rupees Twelve Lakhs Forty SCCH-5 Nine Thousand Six Hundred Twenty Four Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order and recover from the respondent No.2 with due process of law.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, typed by her, thereof is corrected and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 5th day of October, 2024)

(MANJUNATHA K.P.)
